    Chapter 1

    Welcome

    1.1 · What YASDE is

    YASDE (“Yet Another Samsung Dex Emulator”) turns one window on your Linux PC into a desktop. The apps of your Android phone open as windows inside that desktop, and you use them with mouse and keyboard. It is an independent project, not affiliated with Samsung, and it is designed for Android 14 or later phones of any make, using only standard Android. It has been tried on one phone so far.

    The apps keep running on the phone, with their data and accounts. YASDE sends their picture and sound to the PC and sends your clicks and keystrokes back to the phone. With YASDE you can:

    • keep a desktop with a wallpaper, app icons and widgets, and a taskbar with a launcher;
    • open the phone's apps in separate windows, several at the same time;
    • type with the PC keyboard and copy and paste text in both directions;
    • hear the phone's app sound through the PC speakers;
    • read the phone's notifications and see the phone's status on the PC;
    • send files to the phone, download files from it and install an APK;
    • take screenshots and record an app's screen;
    • open a window that mirrors the phone's real screen.
    i
    Nothing to install. no app is installed on the phone and no root access is needed. The few things YASDE changes while it runs are put back when it closes (15.1 “What YASDE changes on the phone”).

    The program is in English only.

    i
    Licence. YASDE is free: anyone may use it, change it and pass it on, but may not sell it. The terms are the MIT License with the Commons Clause condition, in the file LICENSE of the project. The third-party components that come in the package keep their own licences, listed in the documentation folder of the package.

    1.2 · Who this manual is for

    To go from the downloaded file to the first open app, follow 3.3 “Pairing step by step”. The 17.1 “Glossary of terms” explains the less common words.

    1.3 · Conventions

    In this manual “phone” is the Android phone connected to YASDE and “PC” is the Linux computer running it. Names of Android settings, for example Wireless debugging, can differ a little from one brand to another: the manual uses the most common names. The figures that are drawings show the idea. The screenshots were taken with a demonstration phone, with invented apps and data; the content inside the app windows is a placeholder.

    i
    Version. this manual describes YASDE 2.1.0. What it says is checked against the program: if something is not described here, YASDE does not do it.
    Chapter 2

    Installation

    2.1 · What you need

    YASDE is a single file for Linux PCs with an x86-64 processor. There is nothing to install: you download the file, make it executable and start it. The file is about 18 MB and already contains GTK 4 and the video libraries it needs.

    i
    Other systems. the list comes from what the package asks of the system. YASDE has not been tried on every Linux distribution, so a system older than the one described may need more.

    2.2 · Starting YASDE

    1. Download YASDE-2.1-x86_64.AppImage and put it in any folder you like.
    2. Make it executable: in your file manager open the file's properties and allow running it as a program, or type chmod +x YASDE-2.1-x86_64.AppImage in a terminal.
    3. Double-click the file, or run it from a terminal. A single YASDE window opens.
    4. At the first start the window shows Connect your phone: go on with 3.2 “The Connect your phone screen”.
    +
    Full screen. the window can be switched to full screen with the Full screen button in its title bar or with the F11 key (8.2 “Keyboard”).

    2.3 · What YASDE adds to your system

    YASDE does not touch the rest of your system.

    • It adds no menu entry, no launcher and no icon: the file runs from where you put it.
    • Apart from the files you ask for (screenshots, recordings and downloads, 12.1 “Screenshots” and 11.2 “Downloading files from the phone”), it writes on the PC only in two folders: ~/.config/YASDE for settings and the phone's key, and ~/.cache/YASDE for the wallpaper image and a small image-loader file (14.2 “Where YASDE keeps its data”).
    • On the phone it installs nothing (15.1 “What YASDE changes on the phone”).

    2.4 · Updating and removing

    To update, replace the file with the new one. To remove YASDE completely, delete the file and the two folders ~/.config/YASDE and ~/.cache/YASDE. The phone needs no cleaning: whatever YASDE put on it is removed when YASDE closes. To be sure, close YASDE normally with the phone connected before deleting it. If the last session was cut short (for example the Wi-Fi dropped), start YASDE and close it once: it cleans up what was left.

    !
    Settings are lost. deleting ~/.config/YASDE also deletes the key that pairs the PC with the phone, together with your wallpaper, icons and widgets. You will have to pair the phone again.
    Chapter 3

    Connecting the phone

    3.1 · Before you start

    The first connection is done once for each phone, without a cable, in a few minutes. YASDE needs two things on the phone: the Android Developer options and the Wireless debugging switch. After that the phone connects by itself every time.

    • The phone: Android 14 or later, charged and unlocked.
    • The PC and the phone on the same Wi-Fi network (not a guest network that keeps devices apart, and not mobile data).
    • YASDE running: at the first start it shows the Connect your phone screen by itself.
    i
    Where things are. the Android names depend on the brand. The search field in the phone's Settings finds them quickly: type build number or wireless debugging.

    3.2 · The Connect your phone screen

    Until a phone is paired, the whole YASDE window is the connection screen. Its content follows what YASDE sees on the network.

    Above the title the card always shows the name YASDE, “Yet Another Samsung Dex Emulator” and the line “Independent project, not affiliated with Samsung”.

    YASDE works with one phone at a time. It finds phones by listening on the local network, so you never type an address, except in the special case described in 3.5 “If the phone does not show up”.

    3.3 · Pairing step by step

    1. Make sure the phone is on the same Wi-Fi network and that Wireless debugging is on (3.1 “Before you start”).
    2. On the phone open Developer options › Wireless debugging and tap Pair device with pairing code. The phone shows a six-digit code and keeps the pairing screen open.
    3. In a moment the YASDE screen changes to Pair the phone: it says On the phone: Developer options › Wireless debugging › Pair device with pairing code. Type here the six-digit code that appears. and shows the field Pairing code.
    4. Type the six digits (anything that is not a digit is ignored, so a code pasted with spaces works) and press Pair.
    5. The screen shows Pairing in progress… and then Paired: connecting the phone…. When the connection is made the screen disappears and your desktop appears.
    +
    Do not close it. keep the pairing screen on the phone open until YASDE has finished: the code is valid only while that screen is shown.
    i
    The code is not kept. YASDE never saves the pairing code, on disk or in logs. It saves the key of the PC, so the phone recognises it next time, and the phone's last address, used to reconnect (never written in the logs).

    3.4 · Pairing messages

    If the pairing does not go through, YASDE says why under the field:

    The phone does not appear? Turn Wireless debugging off and on again on the phone and press Search again. See also 3.6 “Stuck on Looking for phones on the network”.

    3.5 · If the phone does not show up

    When the Pairing code field is shown but pairing keeps failing, YASDE may not be seeing the phone's pairing service. Open The phone does not show up? Type the address and port under the button and type the IP address and port that the phone shows under the pairing code (for example 192.0.2.10:37123), then press Pair. The button is inactive while the address is not valid.

    i
    Only for pairing. this field appears only on the pairing screen. If you are still on Connect your phone the phone is not announcing itself on the network: turn Wireless debugging off and on.

    3.6 · Stuck on Looking for phones on the network

    The most frequent problem at the first connection is that the screen stays on Looking for phones on the network…. YASDE listens for the phone's announcement on the network; if the phone does not send it, YASDE cannot find it. Try, in this order:

    1. On the phone turn Wireless debugging off and on again. This solved the problem in testing.
    2. Check that phone and PC are on the same Wi-Fi network and that the router does not keep Wi-Fi devices apart (some guest networks do).
    3. Press Search again.

    3.7 · Later connections

    After the first pairing there is nothing more to do. When YASDE starts it looks for the phone on the network and connects by itself, and your desktop comes back as you left it.

    • The phone must be on, on the same Wi-Fi network, with Wireless debugging turned on.
    • Android sometimes turns Wireless debugging off by itself, for example when you change Wi-Fi network. Turn it on again: no new code is needed.
    • If the phone is locked when YASDE connects, the screen says Phone locked until you unlock it (13.4 “A locked phone and a lost connection”).
    • If the phone no longer recognizes this PC (for example you removed it in Developer options), YASDE should show Pair the phone again, and you repeat the pairing. This case has not been tried live.
    +
    Quick turn-on. many phones let you add Wireless debugging to the Quick Settings tiles: it turns back on with one tap.
    Chapter 4

    The desktop

    4.1 · What you see

    Once the phone is connected, the YASDE window is a desktop: a wallpaper, app icons and widgets in the middle, the taskbar at the bottom. App windows open on top of it.

    • The desktop is kept for each phone: wallpaper, icons and widgets are saved automatically and come back at the next start.
    • A new phone starts with a teal gradient wallpaper, no icons and three widgets on the right: Clock, Phone status and Recent notifications.
    • The window can be made smaller or larger, down to 640 × 420, and put in full screen (8.2 “Keyboard”).

    4.2 · The desktop menu

    Right-click an empty part of the desktop to open its menu:

    4.3 · The wallpaper

    The dialog Desktop wallpaper has a preview at the top and three tabs under Wallpaper type. Every change is applied at once; close the dialog with Done.

    i
    A copy on the PC. the chosen picture is copied to the PC (in ~/.cache/YASDE), so the wallpaper stays even when the phone is disconnected. Pictures in JPEG, PNG and WebP are accepted; a picture that is too large or cannot be read gives Wallpaper not changed.

    4.4 · Icons

    Icons are shortcuts to the phone's apps. They sit on a grid and show the app's name.

    • To add one, open the launcher (6.4 “The launcher”) and drag an app onto the desktop, or right-click it there and choose Add to desktop. The message Added to the desktop confirms it.
    • For the best-known apps YASDE uses the icons of the Kora theme; the other apps show the phone's own icon, so the style may be mixed. An app that changes its icon on the phone still shows the Kora one.
    • Click an icon to open the app. Drag it to move it to another free cell: it never opens by accident while dragging.
    • Right-click an icon for Open and Remove from desktop. Removing only deletes the shortcut: the app stays on the phone.
    • When there is no free cell you get Desktop full: Remove an icon to make room.
    +
    Space. widgets are on the right side of the desktop, so icons use only the space that remains. If the window becomes too small for a cell, the icon moves to the nearest free one on screen.
    i
    Credits. the Kora icon theme is the work of bikass (github.com/bikass/kora) and is distributed under the GPL-3. It comes with YASDE as separate files, with the full GPL-3 text and its credits in the documentation folder of the package.
    Chapter 5

    Widgets

    5.1 · Adding and arranging widgets

    Widgets are small cards on the desktop. YASDE draws them on the PC with data it reads from the phone. They are not Android widgets: only the ones in the catalog below exist.

    1. Right-click an empty part of the desktop and choose Add widget….
    2. In the dialog Add widget press Add on the card you want. The message Widget added confirms it. You can add several; close the dialog with Done.
    3. Drag the widget where you want it: it snaps to a grid of 8 pixels.
    4. Right-click a widget to change it (see below).
    • Each widget has three sizes: Small, Medium and Large. Larger sizes show more details.
    • The right-click menu of a widget has Size, Style (for the widgets that have styles), City (for the dual time zone clock), Location… (for the weather) and Remove widget.
    • Size, style and position are saved for each phone.

    5.2 · The catalog

    i
    Not available. three widgets are not in the catalog: Find my phone, Quick notes and Now playing. They are not available in this version.

    5.3 · Styles

    Styles change how a widget looks without changing the data. Choose one from the right-click menu, under Style.

    5.4 · The weather widget

    The Weather widget is the only part of YASDE that uses the Internet, and only while a weather widget is on the desktop.

    • The place comes from the phone's position. YASDE asks the phone, which gives a position rounded to about 500 meters; the precise position never leaves the phone. The name of the place is worked out by Android on the phone from that rounded position; on many phones that uses an online service of Google or of the phone's maker.
    • If the phone does not give a position, the widget says so and offers Choose a location…. The same dialog is under Location… in the widget menu. Type a city in City name and press Search (or Enter): the search is sent only when you press it. Pick a result, or None to forget the city. A city chosen by hand is used only when the phone gives no position.
    • The widget always shows Weather data by Open-Meteo.com and, in the search dialog, Places from GeoNames, via Open-Meteo.com.
    • While data is being fetched you see Updating…; if the service does not answer you see Forecast not available and the words “last data at” followed by a time when older data exists.
    !
    Internet. adding the widget is the choice: there is no consent dialog. Remove the widget and YASDE stops contacting the weather service. Details are in 15.3 “What leaves the PC: the weather”.
    Chapter 6

    The taskbar and the launcher

    6.1 · The taskbar

    The taskbar is the strip at the bottom of the YASDE window. On the left are the launcher and the apps; on the right the file buttons and the system area.

    The taskbar is dark glass; the launcher, the panels, the menus, the dialogs and the widgets are light glass and let you glimpse, blurred, what is behind them. On computers without graphics acceleration they have a plain, almost opaque background. Nothing changes in how they work.

    6.2 · Working with apps on the taskbar

    A click on an app's icon does what you expect:

    Right-click an app's icon for a menu:

    • Close app (only if the app is open): closes the window and removes the app from the phone's recent apps.
    • Pin to taskbar or Unpin from taskbar.

    A pinned app stays on the taskbar even when it is closed, and shows the name the phone gives it. Pins are kept for each phone, in the order you pinned them, up to 16. A seventeenth gives Taskbar full: Unpin an app to make room.

    6.3 · The clock and the calendar

    Click the clock to open a calendar of the current month. The title gives the date, the arrows Previous month and Next month move by a month, Previous year and Next year by a year. It uses the PC's date and shows no events. Click the clock again, press Esc or click elsewhere to close it.

    i
    Events. for events read from the phone use the Month calendar widget (5.2 “The catalog”).

    6.4 · The launcher

    Click App launcher to see all the phone's apps in a grid. The search field has the focus at once: type part of a name and the grid is filtered. No apps found appears when nothing matches.

    The launcher is a panel in the upper middle of the YASDE window, not a full-screen cover: about 60% of the window's width (never narrower than 480 or wider than 960 pixels), just below the top edge, and as tall as its content, up to about three quarters of the space above the taskbar. The search field stays at the top and the grid scrolls. Clicking outside the panel closes it.

    Chapter 7

    App windows

    7.1 · Opening and controlling a window

    Each app opens in its own window inside the YASDE desktop. Opening an app that is already open only brings its window to the front (or restores it if it was minimized). You can have up to 64 windows.

    The buttons are round and show only their symbol until you point at them. The title bar is made of glass: it lets you glimpse, blurred, what is behind the window. On computers without graphics acceleration the title bar is light and opaque; everything else works the same.

    i
    Placement. new windows open slightly offset from each other. With the option “reopen where you were” (14.3 “Settings you can change by hand”) a window comes back at its last place and size.

    7.2 · Moving and resizing

    • To move a window, drag its title bar. You can push it partly outside the left, right and bottom edges to put it aside, but at least 96 pixels and the title bar stay reachable; it never goes above the top edge.
    • To resize, drag the small handle at the bottom-right corner. The minimum is 288 × 180.
    • Click a window to bring it to the front; the active window has a darker name and symbols and a stronger shadow, while the others are dimmed.
    • Rotate (menu More commands, or Ctrl+R) swaps the width and height of a window. It does nothing on a maximized, snapped or fixed-shape window, or while recording.
    • A window you minimize pauses its picture to save work; restoring it resumes at once. The app itself keeps running on the phone.

    While you move or resize, YASDE only scales the picture. The phone is told the new size once you stop moving for about a third of a second.

    7.3 · Snapping windows

    Drag a window by its title bar toward an edge of the desktop and release:

    A snapped window follows the desktop if you resize the YASDE window. Dragging its title bar away unsnaps it and it gets its previous size back.

    7.4 · Windows that cannot be resized

    Some apps are made only for portrait use. YASDE keeps their window in phone shape: they cannot be resized, maximized or snapped, and Rotate is inactive. You can still move, minimize and close them. The window of the phone's mirrored screen (13.3 “The phone screen mirror”) works the same way.

    +
    Size. the app is shown at the size of the phone's screen, reduced if it does not fit the desktop, and never narrower than a phone would make it.

    7.5 · Size and the Compatibility option

    How big an app looks depends on a setting called density. YASDE chooses it for you, window by window, so that one dot of the app is about one pixel of the screen, as on Samsung DeX. A small window therefore looks like a phone; a large window gives the app more room instead of making everything bigger, so an app may switch to a tablet layout. There is no control for this in the interface.

    A few apps draw themselves too small. The cause is in the app: it uses the density of the phone's real screen instead of the one it is given. For these apps YASDE has the Compatibility option:

    1. Open the window of the app and click More commands.
    2. Tick Compatibility (the menu says For apps that look too small).
    3. The app redraws at the right size at once, without being reopened.
    • The choice is remembered for that app, for that phone, and applied each time you open it. Untick it to go back.
    • It is not offered for the phone screen mirror and is inactive while the window is being recorded.
    • Up to 128 apps can have it; beyond that you get Too many apps in compatibility mode..
    Chapter 8

    Mouse, keyboard and clipboard

    8.1 · Mouse and touchpad

    In an app window the mouse acts as one finger on the phone's screen.

    i
    Other buttons. the right and middle buttons reach the app only when you press them on the app's own content. A click in the title bar, on a window border or on a window button works on the window, never on the app. Only one button counts at a time: pressing a second button while one is held cancels what you were doing (a touch is cancelled on the phone; a window move or resize is cancelled) and the second button does nothing. The back and forward buttons of the mouse are not sent. A right or middle click also brings the window to the front, like a left click.

    8.2 · Keyboard

    The window that has the focus receives the keys. Letters, digits, accents and symbols are sent as text, so capitals and your keyboard layout come out right. Enter, Tab, Backspace, Delete, arrows, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down and F1 to F12 are sent as keys, and shortcuts with Ctrl or Alt (such as Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V) are passed to the app.

    These keys never reach the phone (Esc only while it acts as Back). In full screen the title bar is hidden: move the pointer to the top edge and a bar with Exit full screen slides down.

    8.3 · Shared clipboard

    The PC and the phone share their clipboard, for text only.

    • Copy text on the PC and paste it in an app, or the reverse: the text travels by itself, with no extra step.
    • Pictures and files are not shared this way (use 11.1 “Sending files to the phone”).
    • Texts longer than 200,000 bytes are ignored.
    • A copy that a password manager marks as sensitive never passes between the two, in either direction.
    • YASDE never writes the copied text in its logs.
    +
    Screenshots. a screenshot copied with Ctrl+Shift+C goes to the PC clipboard as a picture and is not sent to the phone.
    Chapter 9

    Sound

    9.1 · How the sound reaches the PC

    YASDE sends the sound of the phone's apps to the PC speakers. The sound starts about five seconds after the first app window opens, and stays on while YASDE is connected. If the sound channel drops it is reopened by itself a few times.

    • What is sent: sound of apps and media, games, alarms and notification sounds.
    • What stays on the phone: the audio of phone calls and the ringtone.
    • The sound plays through the PC's normal audio output, in the PipeWire service.
    i
    Synchronized. audio and video are kept in step: a video in a browser plays with its sound aligned.

    9.2 · The volume control

    The Volume: 100% button on the taskbar opens the volume popup.

    The popup says Adjusts YASDE audio on the PC. The phone volume does not change. The slider is a gain applied on the PC. It starts at 100% the first time; afterwards YASDE remembers the last level you set, separately for each phone. The mute is not remembered: YASDE starts with sound on.

    +
    Instant. muting does not stop the sound channel: unmuting is immediate.

    9.3 · What happens to the phone's volume

    To make sure apps start their sound, YASDE raises the phone's media volume to the maximum while it captures sound, and puts it back when it stops.

    • If you change the phone's volume yourself in the meantime, YASDE leaves your value alone.
    • The change is registered for restoration before it is made, so it is undone even if YASDE or the connection fails: at the latest the next time YASDE starts. If the restore cannot be made safe, the volume is not touched.
    • The popup slider never changes the phone's volume.
    Chapter 10

    Notifications and phone status

    10.1 · The notifications panel

    The Notifications button on the taskbar is a bell with the number of notifications you have not hidden. Click it to open the panel Notifications.

    • Each entry shows the app's icon, the title, the text, and the app's name with the time.
    • Click an entry to open its app; the notification is hidden at the same time.
    • Hide hides one notification and Hide all hides them all. When none is left the panel says No notifications.
    • Hiding works only in YASDE: it does not remove the notification from the phone. A hidden notification that the app updates appears again.
    • If the phone cannot give its notifications you see I cannot read the phone's notifications..

    10.2 · Pop-up cards and PC notifications

    When a new notification arrives a card appears at the bottom right for a few seconds. Click it to open the app. Short messages from YASDE itself (for example Widget added or Screenshot saved) use the same card.

    • One message of this kind warns about video: Hardware video decoding unavailable means that YASDE is decoding the video with the processor, so apps look less smooth. It stays on screen longer than the others (about nine seconds) and appears at most once each time the phone connects, if the video falls back to the processor (16.3 “Problems with windows and apps”).
    • Only notifications that arrive while YASDE is connected give a card: the ones already on the phone at connection, or after a reconnection, do not.
    • If the YASDE window is minimized or not in front, a new notification is also sent to your PC's own notification system, so you see it even without looking at YASDE. This can be switched off by hand (14.3 “Settings you can change by hand”).
    • YASDE keeps titles and texts of notifications only in memory, never on disk and never in logs. The PC's own notification system, which receives them with the default setting, may keep a history of them.

    10.3 · The phone popup

    The button Phone status shows the Wi-Fi and battery icons with the battery percentage. Click it for the popup.

    Chapter 11

    Files

    11.1 · Sending files to the phone

    There are three ways to send files from the PC to the phone, all in the panel Send to the phone (From the PC to the phone):

    1. Click Send files to the phone on the taskbar, or just drag files from your file manager over the YASDE window: a frame appears saying Drop to send to the phone, and the files are queued when you release them.
    2. Or press Choose files from the PC to pick files in the system's file dialog.
    3. Check the destination under Destination folder on the phone. The starting folder is Download, or the last one you used. The buttons under Frequently used folders jump to Download, Documents, Pictures and Music.

    To pick another folder press Change…. You get a folder browser for the phone:

    • Up goes to the parent folder; the path field takes a path (Enter goes there; the phone's “/sdcard” is understood).
    • The search field Search for a folder on the whole phone finds folders by name.
    • New folder creates one in the current folder; Use this folder makes it the destination.
    • Hidden folders are not listed, and some places say Access not allowed by the system.
    i
    Folders. only regular files are sent, not folders: if you drop a folder you get Some items were not sent.

    11.2 · Downloading files from the phone

    Click Download files from the phone for the panel Download from the phone (From the phone to the PC).

    1. Browse the phone with Up, the path field or the search field (Search files or folders on the whole phone). It starts at the phone's main storage.
    2. Tick the files with their checkboxes. Your selection stays while you change folder.
    3. Check Destination folder on the PC (starting from your Downloads folder, or the last one used; Change… opens a folder browser of the PC).
    4. Press the large button, which says Select the files to download until you tick something, and then “Download” followed by the number of files.

    11.3 · The transfer list

    Both panels list their transfers, newest first, with the percentage and a bar. States are Waiting, Completed, Cancelled and Failed.

    • Each entry has a cancel button; Cancel all transfers stops the whole queue.
    • A message Sent to the phone or Downloaded to the PC appears when a transfer ends.
    • While a transfer is running the taskbar button shows a dot.
    • If the connection drops, the waiting transfers restart by themselves when it comes back.
    • The widget Recent transfers shows the latest ones on the desktop.

    11.4 · Installing an app from an APK

    Drop an .apk file on the YASDE window and YASDE offers to install it instead of copying it.

    1. A dialog asks Install the app NAME on the phone? and explains that an app already on the phone is replaced and keeps its data.
    2. Press Install the app (or Cancel).
    3. The panel shows Installing on the phone, and at the end App installed on the phone..

    If it fails YASDE says why. The most common messages:

    i
    Temporary file. the temporary copy of the APK that YASDE puts on the phone is removed afterwards; if that fails it is removed at the next connection.
    Chapter 12

    Screenshots and recordings

    12.1 · Screenshots

    To take a screenshot of an app, press Screenshot in its title bar.

    • The picture is saved as a PNG in Pictures/YASDE (your Pictures folder; if you have none, the folder is made in your home folder) and is also copied to the PC clipboard, so you can paste it right away.
    • A message says Screenshot saved with the folder: Pictures/YASDE and copied to the clipboard.
    • To copy only, without a file, press Ctrl+Shift+C (Copy screenshot): you get Screenshot copied to the clipboard.
    • The file is named after the app, the date and the time, for example Browser 2026-11-24 10.30.05.png; if that name exists, (2), (3)… are added. YASDE never overwrites a file.
    i
    Protected apps. some apps protect their screen. For them the window shows This app protects its screen: the content cannot be shown. and a screenshot cannot be taken.

    12.2 · Recordings

    Press Record the screen in the title bar to start recording the window's app, and press it again to stop. REC shows next to the app's name while recording.

    • The recording is an MP4 file in the same folder as the screenshots, named like them. The video is saved as the phone sends it, without being re-encoded.
    • It records the screen only, without sound.
    • At the end you get Recording saved with the folder.
    • It stops by itself, with Recording interrupted, if the window is minimized, if the YASDE window is hidden, if you close the window or if the connection is lost (Recording interrupted: connection lost). What was recorded up to then is kept.
    • While a window records it cannot be resized, maximized, snapped or rotated, and Compatibility is inactive: the picture size must not change.
    • If a recording is already running in that window and you ask for another, you get Recording is already in progress..
    Chapter 13

    The phone's screen

    13.1 · The physical panel

    The apps you see in YASDE run on virtual screens, not on the phone's real display. So the real screen can stay off while you work on the PC. Only the light of the panel is switched off: Android believes the screen is on, and the apps keep running.

    • Right after the connection succeeds YASDE turns the panel off, once. If the phone refuses (it is locked or in a call), it does not insist.
    • If you take the phone in hand and touch its screen, press a button, unlock it, or a call arrives or is in progress, the panel turns on by itself and stays on while you use the phone.
    • At the first input you give from the PC after that, the panel turns off again.
    • If the phone was already “in hand” at the moment of the connection, the panel is not turned off.
    • Closing the last app window does not turn the panel on again. It comes back on only if you unlock or touch the phone, at a call, when you use the switch below, or when YASDE closes.
    i
    Dark, not asleep. while the panel is off the phone's display is dark but the phone is awake. Touching the dark screen wakes it, as you expect.

    13.2 · Phone awake and unlocked

    While YASDE is connected the phone does not go to sleep and does not lock because of inactivity, even if you only watch a video on the PC. YASDE does it with an Android “keep awake” request that the phone drops by itself if YASDE dies.

    • If you lock the phone yourself with its power button, it locks: that is your choice and YASDE does not fight it (13.4 “A locked phone and a lost connection”).
    • If the PC disappears without YASDE closing (for example the Wi-Fi drops), the phone waits 30 minutes with no sign from the PC. Then it goes back to normal: panel on, your own screen timeout, and it locks with its usual timing.
    • When the PC comes back, the phone is meant to be kept awake again, with the panel on until YASDE turns it off at the next input. This case has not been tried live.
    • When YASDE closes or crashes the phone returns to its normal behavior.

    13.3 · The phone screen mirror

    Click Show the phone screen in the phone popup to open a window titled Phone screen that mirrors the real screen of the phone. Click it again to close the window.

    • The mirror has a fixed shape, the proportion of the phone's screen. It moves, minimizes and closes like the other windows, but cannot be resized or maximized, and has no Compatibility option.
    • Mouse and keyboard work in it as in the other windows.

    13.4 · A locked phone and a lost connection

    YASDE follows the phone's lock state.

    The desktop is hidden behind a veil in these cases and returns when the phone is back.

    Chapter 14

    Settings and where YASDE keeps its data

    14.1 · What YASDE remembers

    YASDE has no settings window. What you arrange (wallpaper, icons, widgets, pinned apps, volume, folders) is saved by itself, for each phone, and comes back at the next start. A few options exist only as lines in a file you can edit by hand.

    14.2 · Where YASDE keeps its data

    Besides the files you ask for (screenshots and recordings in Pictures/YASDE, downloads in your Downloads folder or the one you chose), YASDE writes on the PC only in two folders, which follow the XDG rules (if you set XDG_CONFIG_HOME or XDG_CACHE_HOME to an absolute path, those are used instead of ~/.config and ~/.cache).

    • Files are written safely: if the PC loses power during a save, you keep either the old file or the new one, never half of one. The folder is private to you.
    • A file that cannot be read is not erased: it is renamed with the ending .illeggibile and YASDE starts with default values.
    • Wallpaper pictures that no phone file uses any more are removed from the cache at start.
    i
    Cache in memory. on some systems ~/.cache is in memory and is emptied at each restart. Then a picture used as wallpaper is lost, and the wallpaper must be chosen again.

    14.3 · Settings you can change by hand

    Close YASDE before editing a file: it saves its own copy when it closes and would overwrite yours. The files are plain text with lines such as name = value under headings in square brackets. The names are in Italian.

    preferenze.toml: the options and their default values
    [generale]
esc_indietro = true
avvisi = true
cartella_ricevuti = ""
widget_nascosti = false
riapri_dove_eri = false

[shell]
scala_automatica = true
scala = 1.0

    The line lingua is read and ignored: the program is always in English.

    Chapter 15

    Privacy and what changes on the phone

    15.1 · What YASDE changes on the phone

    YASDE installs nothing on the phone and needs no root. Everything below is temporary and is undone when YASDE closes, except where the table says otherwise; if the connection is cut, at the latest at the next start of YASDE.

    15.2 · Restoring the phone

    Each change to a phone setting (panel, screen timeout, refresh rate, volume) is first registered with a small guardian program on the phone, then made. If YASDE or the connection fails, the guardian restores the phone.

    • If Wireless debugging is turned off and on while YASDE is running, Android may stop the guardian too, and the restore waits. At the next start YASDE carries out any pending restore and removes the leftovers.
    • If YASDE cannot make a restore safe, it does not make the change.
    !
    Your changes win. If you changed the screen timeout or the volume yourself while YASDE was running, YASDE leaves your new value.

    15.3 · What leaves the PC: the weather

    The only connection to the Internet is the weather widget, and only while a Weather widget is on the desktop. The rest of the traffic between PC and phone goes over your local network, but see the note on the place name below.

    • The rounding is done on the phone: the precise position never leaves it. The name of the place is worked out on the phone by Android's own geocoder from the rounded coordinates; on many phones that is an online service of Google or of the phone's maker, which YASDE does not control.
    • Both services also see the PC's Internet address, as any website does.
    • The position is not saved on disk and not written in logs. The only place saved is a city you chose by hand (name and rounded coordinates, in the phone's file).
    • There is no consent dialog: adding the widget is the choice. Remove it and nothing is sent. The widget shows “Weather data by Open-Meteo.com”, a free service for non-commercial use.
    • Pairing and everything else between PC and phone travels on the local Wi-Fi network in an encrypted connection.

    15.4 · What YASDE keeps

    • The pairing code is never saved. The phone's last address is saved in telefoni.toml to reconnect, and is never written in logs.
    • YASDE keeps notification titles and texts, and copied text, only in memory. With the default setting, though, a new notification is also handed to the PC's own notification system when YASDE is not in front, and that system may keep a history of it.
    • Copies marked sensitive by a password manager are never passed between PC and phone.
    • On the PC disk YASDE keeps the phone's serial number (in a file name and in telefoni.toml), its name, its last address, your wallpaper picture and your layout.

    Chapter 17

    Glossary

    17.1 · Glossary of terms

    Words used in this manual.

    ADB
    Android Debug Bridge, the connection method Android offers to computers. YASDE speaks it itself: no Android tools are needed on the PC.
    APK
    The file of an Android app.
    AppImage
    A single file that runs on Linux without installing anything.
    Back
    Android's “go back” action: the Back button of a window and the Esc key.
    Compatibility
    A per-app option that makes apps drawn too small use the real density of the phone's screen.
    Density
    How many dots Android draws in an inch. It decides how large an app looks. YASDE sets it for each window.
    Developer options
    A hidden section of the phone's Settings that you unlock by tapping Build number seven times.
    Guardian
    A small helper on the phone that puts things back if YASDE or the connection dies.
    In hand
    The state of the phone when you touch it, unlock it or use it for a call: its screen is on and YASDE does not turn it off until you work from the PC again.
    Launcher
    The grid with all the apps of the phone.
    Mirror
    The window titled Phone screen that shows the real screen of the phone.
    Open-Meteo
    The free weather service used by the Weather widget.
    Pairing code
    The six digits shown by the phone to authorize the PC.
    Physical panel
    The light-emitting part of the phone's screen. YASDE can turn it off while the phone stays awake.
    Pin
    To keep an app's icon on the taskbar even when it is closed.
    Snapping
    Dragging a window to an edge of the desktop so that it fills a half or the whole area.
    Taskbar
    The bar at the bottom with the launcher, the open apps and the system buttons.
    Veil
    A cover over the desktop that says the phone is locked or the connection was lost.
    Virtual screen
    A screen that exists only in memory. The apps in YASDE windows run on virtual screens, not on the phone's display.
    Wake lock
    An Android request to keep the phone awake; it is released by Android when the program that asked dies.
    Widget
    A small card on the desktop that shows data from the phone or the PC.
    Wireless debugging
    The Android setting that lets the PC connect over Wi-Fi.
